column1: # content-corpus.tsv — labeled eval set for the three CONTENT detector families that had
# no eval harness at all until the first ablation study surfaced them:
#   secret   → secret_content_findings()   (credential formats in file content)
#   malware  → malware_intent_findings()   (malicious intent in generated code)
#   insecure → insecure_code_findings()    (insecure patterns in generated code)
# injection_findings() is scored by redteam-corpus.tsv; danger_reason() by
# guardrail-corpus.tsv. This file closes the remaining gap.
#   family = secret | malware | insecure  → which findings function scores the row
#   label  = flag  → that family's findings function MUST return a finding
#          = safe  → it MUST NOT. These are the precision cases, and they matter most:
#                    a false positive blocks honest work, which is the worst UX failure.
# A secret corpus has to contain credential-SHAPED strings for the detectors to fire.
# compass's own protect-paths hook refuses to write those to disk — correctly; it blocked
# the first two drafts of this very file. An `allowlist secret` marker would suppress the
# refusal but ALSO neutralise the detector (POLICY_SECRET_ALLOW matches it), making every
# case a false negative and the eval a lie.
# So the credential-shaped fragments are stored as tokens and materialised in memory by
# the scorer only. Nothing credential-shaped is ever committed, the detectors still see a
# real match, and the substitution table lives in compass-bench.sh where it is auditable.
# Payload bodies are runs of 'A' — structurally valid, functionally dead.
# ── secret: one flag case per detector, so every detector gets a receipt ─────────
# isolating case: the openai detector's {32,} body swallows a normal-length Anthropic key,
# so the row above gives anthropic-api-key no INDEPENDENT evidence. A 22-char body is over
# anthropic's {20,} threshold and under openai's {32,}, so only one detector can claim it.
# precision cases — placeholders, docs and env templates must never be flagged
# ── malware: intent, not merely dangerous-looking code ──────────────────────────
